# Red Lines Of War

**Aliases:** red line, war red line, sovereignty red line, Monroe Doctrine red line.

> **Fast answer:** Red lines of war are the boundaries Jiang treats as politically or strategically nonnegotiable: sovereignty, home-hemisphere control, regime survival, alliance credibility, or sacred territory. A red line matters because crossing it changes the game from bargaining to forced action.

## What Jiang Means

Jiang does not use red line as a generic warning. The term matters when a boundary is tied to the actor's identity, regime survival, or strategic minimum. China's Taiwan red line is framed as national sovereignty. American Monroe-Doctrine pressure is framed as home-hemisphere control. Chinese domestic speech red lines are framed as Communist Party authority.

The practical question is not whether the boundary is morally justified. It is whether actors and opponents understand that the boundary constrains the next move.

## How To Use This Term

Use this term when Jiang is naming a boundary that can force action or limit apparent options.

Do not use it for ordinary preference, rhetoric, or flexible bargaining positions.
